findings.title: Saved-package verification does not verify the saved shader graph
findings.details: Verify checks blend/usage flags, material assignment and texture import settings but never inspects material property inputs, texture references or specular value. A saved material whose Normal is disconnected, BaseColor points to a different texture, ORM channels are swapped, or gain0.25 is applied again still passes and receives a new trusted package hash. This fails to prove the accepted baked recipe survived saving.
findings.suggestion: Check actual saved MP_BASE_COLOR/NORMAL/AO/ROUGHNESS/METALLIC input nodes, exact texture identity/sampler/output channels and specular constant0.35; reject any extra gain/normal-strength node.

findings.title: Publisher trusts the old empty runtime_data_changes list rather than rechecking verified Data
findings.details: The verification report records only Data count and an empty during-command change list, not its baseline hashes. Publisher checks that old list, then reads whatever current stonebrook.json exists. A floor transform/collision/light/warp or another Data file can change after native verification while publication still reports verified unchanged runtime data. The reverted==baseline assertion compares against current bytes and does not detect this intervening drift.
findings.suggestion: Include complete Data path/hash set in verify report and revalidate immediately before publication. Preserve intended idempotence by explicitly canonicalizing the57already-published mesh refs or requiring a matching prior publication receipt; do not waive other Data drift.
